what: A P&L-BLIND density gate on Kalshi market making: quote a market only if its SERIES has at least N trading markets in the selection window. N chosen on the TRAIN split, applied unchanged to the TEST split. Every figure is produced by app.scripts.mm_backtest's own replay/_block/_split/cluster_bootstrap; the gate is applied by replacing a refused market's MarketRow with the harness's own declined row (quote_hours=0, n_fills=0, pnl=0.0), never by re-implementing P&L.

rule.statement: Quote a market only if its SERIES has at least N trading markets in the selection window.
rule.why: density counts markets, never dollars; no rule here names a series

provenance.event_overlap_source: reports/kalshi-honest-holdout.json overlap.event_overlap, verified there by raw json.load of both cache files
provenance.gate_application: refused markets are replaced by MarketRow(quote_hours=0, n_fills=0, pnl=0.0, markout_pnl=0.0, collateral_mean=0.0, terminal_inventory=0.0) -- the harness's own encoding of a market the policy declined. They stay in the row list so the event set is unchanged and two_split_rule's same-event-set invariant holds.

headline.verdict: The density gate does NOT beat quoting everything. N*=2 was chosen on the train split by the pre-declared rule; on the test split it turns T20's +$400.67 / ROC +5.10% / CI [+0.0365,+0.8615] into +$155.65 / ROC +2.86% / CI [-0.2398,+0.6262]. The CI no longer clears zero and the ROC is lower. The kit's two-split rule also refuses it: N>=2 wins 0 of 60 event-halves and is never once selected by a tuning half. Branch 3 of the fixed interpretation.
headline.the_density_structure_was_not_a_signal: The 20+ bucket that generated the hypothesis is, on this test window, exactly two series -- KXITFMATCH and KXITFWMATCH, both ITF tennis. A gate that selects on density lands on the same two series a gate that named them would have. Remove either one and the N>=20 interval stops clearing zero (minus KXITFWMATCH: [-0.8469,+2.7565]). The optimistic fill model, on the same rows, does not clear zero at N>=20 at all ([-0.1923,+2.5620]) while the pessimistic one does -- two fill models disagreeing about significance at the same N is what noise looks like.
headline.the_one_gate_that_passes_changes_no_pnl: N>=1 -- decline series that take no fills at all in the window -- passes the two-split rule head to head at 55/60 (91.7%, the exact value the harness docstring names as the minimum that clears 90%) with a temporal win, and lifts ROC from +5.10% to +5.77%. It moves P&L by exactly $0.00: total stays +$400.67 and n_trading stays 919, because a market that fills makes its own series dense enough to admit itself. The whole gain is a smaller denominator -- 1,383 quoted markets instead of 1,581, $6,941 of tied collateral instead of $7,858. It is also not what the train split chose, and its strictly causal form (density from the train window only) admits three series and 20 trading markets in the entire test split.

branches_fixed_in_advance: gated test CI clears zero AND two-split rule passes AND the gain over ungated survives the multiplicity -> real improvement, recommend at that N
CI clears zero but two-split fails, or the gain is within multiplicity -> a lead, not a finding
the gate does not beat ungated -> say so plainly; quote-everything wins

anchor_ungated_vs_t20.note: T20 reported, for the shipped params on the pessimistic temporal TEST split: n_trading=919, n_events_trading=789, mean=+0.4360, total=+400.67, roc=+0.0510, ci95=[+0.0365,+0.8615]. Reproduced here from the same cache before any gate is applied; a mismatch would mean this script is not measuring T20's object.

choosing_N_on_train.objective: app.scripts.mm_calibrate._return_on_capital -- total cash pnl / (n_quoted * mean collateral per quoted market), the kit's own two-split objective
choosing_N_on_train.declared_before_the_numbers: N* = the admissible N maximising train return-on-capital, ties broken toward the LARGER N (the stricter gate is the more falsifiable claim). Admissible means the gated train split keeps >= 30 trading markets AND >= 5 trading events, so the objective sits on a sample the harness would put an interval around.

test_split_by_N.note: scored_split is the brief's own wording and is CONTEMPORANEOUS, not causal: it requires knowing at quote time how many markets the series will trade over the window. full_sample is the window handed to two_split_rule, because that function takes one fixed ReplayResult per candidate and partitions it itself, so the gate must be partition-invariant. train_only is the strictly causal version and is reported whatever it does to n.

test_split_by_N_optimistic_crosscheck.note: GUARDRAILS.md 2.2: pessimistic is the verdict; this column is shown beneath it so a reader can see the two models do not disagree in sign.

two_split_rule.rule: PLAN.md 'A default changes on thin evidence': a challenger must win >= 90% of 60 random event-halves AND the temporal test. Both required.
two_split_rule.why_full_sample: two_split_rule takes ONE fixed ReplayResult per candidate and draws its own event-halves from it, so the gate has to be a property of the market, not of the half. full_sample is the only partition-invariant window.

counted.t20_grid_note: T20's two-split rule scored all 48 grid points on 60 random event-halves drawn from this same cache, of which the test window is 93% of the markets; only the winner's temporal-test ROC was computed. Those 48 are not 48 looks at the temporal test split, but they are 48 looks at the data the temporal test split is 93% of.
counted.t22_gate_variants_detail: 7 thresholds [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30] x 3 density windows (scored_split, full_sample, train_only)

what_it_does_to_a_hairline_ci.method: Descriptive only. app.scripts.calibration.cluster_bootstrap is fixed at 95% and takes no alpha, and this task does not re-implement inference, so no corrected interval is computed. What follows is arithmetic about the PROCEDURE, not a second estimator.
what_it_does_to_a_hairline_ci.independence_caveat: These variants are NESTED subsets of one row set, so they are strongly positively correlated and the effective number of independent looks is well below the count. The figure above is therefore an upper bound on the inflation, not an estimate of it. What is NOT in doubt is that the number of looks exceeds one, and both intervals that clear zero clear it by a hair: see lower_bound_as_share_of_mean.

capital_picture.note: total_collateral_implied_usd = n_quoted * collateral_mean, which is exactly the denominator of the harness's roc. It is the capital tied up by a quoted market on average, not a simultaneous peak.

scale.note: Whether this is a business or a rounding error, at the capital it requires.

ungated.ci_note: the per-365-day interval is the event-clustered CI on mean P&L per trading market, scaled by this window's own n_trading and stretched to a year. It assumes the window repeats; it is a scale statement, not a forecast.

gate_N>=20_scored_split.ci_note: the per-365-day interval is the event-clustered CI on mean P&L per trading market, scaled by this window's own n_trading and stretched to a year. It assumes the window repeats; it is a scale statement, not a forecast.

gate_N>=1_scored_split.ci_note: the per-365-day interval is the event-clustered CI on mean P&L per trading market, scaled by this window's own n_trading and stretched to a year. It assumes the window repeats; it is a scale statement, not a forecast.

density_buckets_reproduced.note: The table this task was handed as a HYPOTHESIS, recomputed here from the same cache so the reader can see it is the same object. It is a read of TEST-split P&L and is not evidence for anything; the gate above is the test.

series_admitted_by_the_strict_gates.note: Named as a DIAGNOSTIC of how few independent things the strict gates are betting on -- not as a rule. No gate in this report names a series.

strict_gate_fragility.note: N>=20 admits two series; this is what each one is carrying.
